issues.legal_issue: When review of a decision dismissing a second appeal reveals an error in a survey measurement and further factual consideration is needed, the reviewing court may reopen its own judgment but should preserve the lower courts’ judgments and obtain findings on additional issues arising from the pleadings before disposing of the second appeal.
material_facts: The trial court and first appellate court had concurred in fixing the property boundary using one of two competing commissioner’s plans, and the High Court had dismissed the second appeal.

The review judge noticed that a measurement in the government survey plan, which supported the plan accepted by the lower courts, was erroneous and considered that the competing plans and the position of a survey stone needed further consideration.
The review judge set aside the High Court’s judgment and the judgments of both lower courts and remanded the suit for fresh disposal.
The parties had not produced their title deeds, and the Supreme Court considered that additional issues arising from the pleadings could be framed and evidence received from both parties.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s order was upheld insofar as it set aside its own second-appeal judgment, but was set aside insofar as it vacated the lower courts’ judgments and remanded the suit. Those judgments and decrees were kept intact. The High Court was directed to frame any legally arising additional issues, obtain trial-court findings after allowing both parties to adduce evidence, and then dispose of the second appeal considering those findings, the existing judgments, and any objections.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 47 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the High Court’s decision to set aside its own second-appeal judgment was left undisturbed in these circumstances. Where further factual consideration is needed, the equitable and just procedure is to frame additional issues strictly arising from the pleadings and call for trial-court findings, with both parties permitted to adduce evidence, rather than set aside the concurrent lower-court judgments and remand the suit for fresh disposal. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: second_appeal_review and survey_measurement_error and further_factfinding_needed and additional_issues_arise_from_pleadings

predicates.second_appeal_review: A court considered a review petition concerning its dismissal of a second appeal.
predicates.survey_measurement_error: The reviewing court noticed that a survey measurement relevant to the boundary determination was erroneous.
predicates.further_factfinding_needed: The reviewing court considered further factual consideration necessary to resolve the boundary dispute.
predicates.additional_issues_arise_from_pleadings: The parties’ pleadings could support additional issues for trial-court findings, with both parties permitted to adduce evidence.

issues.definition: When a review of a second-appeal decision reveals a relevant survey-measurement error and further fact-finding on issues arising from the pleadings is needed, the reviewing court may reopen its own judgment but must preserve the lower-court judgments and obtain additional findings before deciding the appeal.
